topic: Unlocking the Geometry of Networks: Planar Graphs and Euler’s Formula
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

outline.topic: Unlocking the Geometry of Networks: Planar Graphs and Euler’s Formula
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: Prerequisites: What is a Planar Graph?
sections.content: Define a planar graph as a graph that can be drawn on a 2D plane without any edges crossing. Introduce the concept of 'Faces' (the enclosed regions including the infinite outer region).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Tetrahedron' graph: show it being flattened into a 2D shape where edges are pushed apart to avoid crossing.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Euler's Characteristic Formula
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental relationship: V - E + F = 2, where V = vertices, E = edges, and F = faces. Explain that this holds for all connected planar graphs.
sections.example: An animation of a simple triangle (V=3, E=3, F=2) showing: 3 - 3 + 2 = 2.

sections.title: Dual Graphs: The Concept of Reflection
sections.content: Explain the dual graph construction: place a point in each face of the original graph and connect points if the faces share an edge. This shows how duals swap vertices and faces.
sections.example: A 'Honeycomb' structure (the original graph) transforming into a 'Triangular Mesh' (its dual graph) as nodes connect across the center of each hexagon.

sections.title: Practical Application: The Map Coloring Challenge
sections.content: Demonstrate why Euler’s formula is critical for spatial constraints, such as the Four Color Theorem, using the dual graph concept to simplify map complexity.
sections.example: Representing a map of a fictional island with 4 regions as a graph, then drawing its dual to find the most efficient way to place communication towers.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the invariance of V - E + F = 2 and the reciprocal nature of dual graphs. Connect this back to the geometric intuition of why 'space' is restricted in planar networks.
sections.example: A quick visual 'speed-run' showing a complex network collapsing into its dual and confirming the calculation remains true throughout the transformation.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: What is a Planar Graph?
lecture_lines: Planar graphs avoid edge crossings on a plane.
Faces are enclosed regions, including the infinite exterior.
animations: Fade in a simple graph with nodes (color #FF5733) and edges (color #33FF57).
Highlight edges (color #33FF57) to show they do not cross.
Flash graph to label it 'Planar' (color #FFFFFF) near the graph.

storyboard.title: The Core Concept: Euler's Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula links vertices, edges, and faces.
The relationship is V minus E plus F equals 2.
This constant holds for all connected planar graphs.
Test it on a triangle: 3 vertices, 3 edges, 2 faces.
animations: Display V - E + F = 2 in center (#FFFFFF).
Animate V, E, and F labels pointing to corresponding graph elements (#FF5733, #33FF57, #5733FF).
Flash the formula (color #FFFF00) to emphasize the invariant.

storyboard.title: Dual Graphs: The Concept of Reflection
lecture_lines: Dual graphs reflect a graph's underlying structure.
Place points in faces; connect across edges.
Duals effectively swap vertices and faces.
Honeycomb structures map to triangular meshes.
Reflect the topology to gain new perspective.
animations: Show original graph with nodes (#FF5733) and edges (#33FF57).
Display new vertices in each face and draw dual edges (#FFFF00).
Pulse original edges (#33FF57) and dual edges (#FFFF00) to show correspondence.

storyboard.title: Practical Application: The Map Coloring Challenge
lecture_lines: Euler's formula helps solve complex spatial constraints.
Dual graphs simplify map coloring challenges.
Model regions as graphs for efficient tower placement.
animations: Show a map with regions colored red, green, blue, yellow.
Assign each region a vertex and draw edges between adjacent regions.
Animate coloring the graph vertices using 4 colors (#FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF, #FFFF00).

storyboard.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Euler's characteristic is an invariant property.
Dual graphs provide deep reciprocal geometric insight.
Geometric space limits network connectivity possibilities.
animations: Display the planarity condition (V-E+F=2) on the left.
Show the dual graph construction on the right.
Highlight the connection between map coloring and planar graphs.
